subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford has walls, a market square, smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense. Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.

subject: bronze-cast forearm
fact: A bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar, not holding anything.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. Not holding anything. Just a hand.

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years, died in Daggerford breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Dwarven inscription
fact: The Dwarven inscription on the base reads: 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the base. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Common inscription
fact: The Common inscription on the back reads: 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.' Signed by Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Common. *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.* Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument two years after the war.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: Small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, charm-sized, sold for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway — walking in very pleased with himself and carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized. He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel, head of a publisher and member of the Order of the Gauntlet, personally signed the monument's inscription.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet. Milo had personally signed off on this.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the group paused before entering, after noting the monument.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later. But we didn't go straight in...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum dropped a gold piece for a pewter hand cast and asked the priest why the Stroudite inscription remained on a Bahamutian paladin's monument.
source_quote: Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his. Then Grygum asked him to tell him more — he'd already paid, so he had the leverage — and the priest was very willing. 'The inscription shares language with Stroud. Why is that?'

subject: Priest of Bahamut
fact: The priest claimed to be a pure Bahamutian and conceded the inscription was a gift left in place because Tarvis saved everyone regardless of the chess game.
source_quote: He himself was, he wanted us to know, *a pure Bahamutian*. He did not believe in the heresy. 'It was a gift,' he said finally. 'And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?'

subject: Maerith of the Ford
fact: Maerith of the Ford is the home of Elin, a 7-year-old girl who has been silent for six days and draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: Maerith of the Ford had the look of a woman who had already been turned away... 'My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface. She talks in her sleep.'

subject: six-pointed star
fact: Elin draws a six-pointed star over and over on every flat surface in her home.
source_quote: Yes, she'd noted the drawings — a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin spoke after Lesser Restoration: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer, the sentient sword, performed Lesser Restoration on Elin, enabling her speech.
source_quote: Dawnbringer could help. Dawnbringer did not wait for a second invitation. 'Let me bring the light to you.' Lesser restoration settled in.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has been experiencing pressure in his head, possibly linked to the same phenomenon affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is named for a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior, and the south wall still bears the memory of his death.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued... 'That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.'

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum, the gnome innkeeper, has maintained the Burning Wizard Inn for thirty years and remembers the story of the burned wizard.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper, old enough to have heard the story from the people who told it first — pointed to the south wall without prompting...

subject: The Kenku Could Not Fly
fact: The bard's song 'The Kenku Could Not Fly' includes the lyric: 'The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed.'
source_quote: This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'... 'The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed, said the small, wise man at his side.'

subject: Whistler
fact: Whistler, the Kenku thief, took only what was necessary from Tiamat’s hoard, forming a line-item budget.
source_quote: The Kenku thief of some earlier age who, presented with the complete hoard of Tiamat, had apparently taken only what was necessary for legitimate expenses. Operating goals. Day-to-day funds. Per diems.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed that Whistler’s restraint mapped well onto his own philosophy.
source_quote: Grygum, who has an irritating habit of noticing things I would have preferred to notice first, observed drily that the song's principle — steal what was needed — mapped rather well onto Whistler.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar whose interest in Stroud is performed slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and he offered a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.
source_quote: Grygum leaned forward — he has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the one who confirmed to Glabbagool that watching the spy is pre-monk training — and Glabbagool accepted the assignment with complete seriousness.
source_quote: "Absolutely," I said. It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it. If anything, the spy was giving him a better curriculum than most of what I'd sat through. Glabbagool took this with complete seriousness.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool asked Zalthir directly: 'Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' — and received an affirmative answer.
source_quote: Glabbagool paused, and asked me directly: "Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?"

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire asked Zalthir: 'What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?' — and later stated: 'I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.'
source_quote: Khell-Vire opened with the question. "What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?" ... Then Khell-Vire set the terms clearly: "There are monks here in the inner ward who have read everything and fought nothing. They will want to test you. Let them. You will learn what you do not see, and they will learn what cannot be read. I will not be there. This is your work, not mine."

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk told Zalthir: 'You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did. Show me what else you haven't learned.'
source_quote: The blind monk entered without introduction and said: "Give me a standard shadow step." ... Then he paused. "You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did. Show me what else you haven't learned."

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk told Zalthir after his failed demonstrations: 'You have learned nothing.'
source_quote: He rolled catastrophically. He fell. The monk watched him fall — insofar as a blind man watches anything — and said, without apparent emotion: "You have learned nothing."

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake — a building that centuries have shaped into something that sits there.
source_quote: Candlekeep is visible from miles out — a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake. I'd seen it described in documents we'd carried out of the Underdark. Seeing it in person was different. It sat there. Centuries do that to a building.

subject: Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall's stone corridors return sound slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.
source_quote: The Echoing Hall earned its name. Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Candlekeep Bell Tower
fact: The bell tower has cells — comfortable, localized anti-magic — rarely used, because Candlekeep holds prisoners but does not keep them.
source_quote: The bell tower has cells. Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used. Anyone we find guilty of a major offense is exiled rather than imprisoned. Which is to say, we hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: The Note on Khell-Vire's Desk
fact: The note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.' — neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire could place it.
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Zalthir stared at it. Khell-Vire stared at it. Neither of them could place it.

subject: The Spy's Bag
fact: The bag contained Glabbagool and a miniaturized House T'sarran spy — which Gate Warden Kalan Strongbranch found unacceptable.
source_quote: When we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him, which she apparently found unacceptable.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir was tested by a blind monk who judged his shadow techniques as technically wrong — yet acknowledged his superior speed and asked him to show what else he hadn't learned.
source_quote: The blind monk ... said: "You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did. Show me what else you haven't learned."

subject: The Decision to Keep the Spy
fact: Candlekeep's Gate Warden Kalan Strongbranch offered only a delay — not imprisonment or execution — and declared that if the party needed something else, they would need to do it themselves.
source_quote: He laid out Candlekeep's position without apology: "... we will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her. Eventually, we will release her at our gate with a warning. If you need something else, you will need to do it yourselves."

subject: Glabbagool's Acceptance of the Spy as Curriculum
fact: Glabbagool, after being told by Zalthir that watching the spy was pre-monk training, drew himself up and declared: 'I will keep an eye on her!' — with six pseudo-eyes fixed on her simultaneously.
source_quote: Glabbagool took this with complete seriousness. The work counted; he had been told so. He drew himself up, or the ooze equivalent of it. "I will keep an eye on her!" Six pseudo-eyes fixed on the spy simultaneously.

subject: The Blind Monk's Final Judgment
fact: After Zalthir failed all three formal techniques, the blind monk sighed and walked away — declaring Zalthir had learned nothing.
source_quote: He tried stealth for the Eldritch Claw. His number landed somewhere that would have been insufficient even with generous interpretation. The monk sighed again and walked away.

subject: The Question of the Broken Mirror
fact: Khell-Vire asked Zalthir: 'Does this phrase mean anything to you that you have lived through that resonates with the phrase?' — and Zalthir replied: 'Not particularly.'
source_quote: Perhaps if I asked it differently — does this phrase mean anything to you that you have lived through that resonates with the phrase?" "Not particularly."

subject: Candlekeep Lower-Gallery Office
fact: The lower-gallery office holds the Shadow Discipline Lineage Records — and Khell-Vire lives among them, wearing a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray.
source_quote: Zalthir had been directed to the lower-gallery office, where the Shadow Discipline Lineage Records were kept, and where a man named Khell-Vire apparently lived among them. He wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray...

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne was assigned as Daz's handler at Candlekeep — without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony. Daz to Sister Yvenne.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire is two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.
source_quote: Two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the Gate Warden who laid out Candlekeep’s official policy on prisoners — and declared: 'We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.'
source_quote: Gate Warden. He was efficient about it. He laid out Candlekeep's position without apology: "... we hold prisoners. We do not keep them."

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the First Reader — a dragonborn sage — who assigned handlers at Candlekeep's gate without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz went quiet beside Zalthir around the second hour of walking — his hand went to his temple and stayed there.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked whether Glabbagool had thoughts on the matter — and observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.
source_quote: Thorin, who processes things by talking, asked whether Glabbagool had thoughts on the matter. ... Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth was assigned as Grygum's handler at Candlekeep — without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony. Grygum to Vareth.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon
fact: Master Archivist Philemon was assigned as Thorin's handler at Candlekeep — without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony. Thorin to Master Archivist Philemon.

subject: The Spy's Attempted Murder of Glabbagool
fact: The spy kept trying to kill Glabbagool — he'd slap her around, she'd try to run, he'd expand, she'd scream, he'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation — she'd scream about the meditation.
source_quote: She kept trying to kill him. He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream. He'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation. She'd scream about the meditation.

subject: The Final Exchange Between Zalthir and the Blind Monk
fact: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk — and he did — and the sparring match that followed was evenly balanced.
source_quote: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk. ... He could. He did. The sparring match that followed was, by all observation, evenly balanced...

subject: The Question of the Bone King
fact: The note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.' — a phrase neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire could place.
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Zalthir stared at it. Khell-Vire stared at it. Neither of them could place it.

subject: The Decision to Keep the Spy
fact: The First Reader told the spy that the decision to keep or release her was not hers — it was the party's — as a guest and member of the adventuring party.
source_quote: The First Reader looked at her with something that might have been sympathy and explained that as a guest of Candlekeep — as a member, technically, of our adventuring party — the decision was ours, not hers.

subject: Candlekeep's South Wall
fact: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat — the wall remembers.
source_quote: Festrum wiped the bar. The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat.

subject: Candlekeep's Floor
fact: The floor was scrubbed every season — a ritual of maintenance.
source_quote: The floor, scrubbed every season.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said to Glabbagool: 'Absolutely' — confirming that watching the spy was pre-monk training.
source_quote: "Absolutely," I said. It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said to the blind monk: 'I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?' — after Thorin asked if he could blindside the monk while walking away.
source_quote: Thorin, from the side: "Can he attack him while he's walking away? Blindside him, as it were?" Zalthir: "I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?"

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said: 'I've played this game before, my friends' — referring to shadow monk pedagogy stretching back five centuries.
source_quote: "I've played this game before, my friends," Zalthir said, which was directed at no one in particular, or possibly at us, or possibly at the entire tradition of shadow monk pedagogy stretching back five centuries.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz's silence and hand-to-temple gesture were noticed by Zalthir — but Zalthir did not say anything yet.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there. I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: The Shadow Monk Trial
fact: The blind monk tested Zalthir on three techniques: the Weightless Shadow, the Efficient Strike, the Eldritch Claw — and judged all three as failures.
source_quote: Then came the formal demonstration. Three techniques: the Weightless Shadow, the Efficient Strike, the Eldritch Claw. The monk had the rubric. Zalthir had to execute against it.

subject: The Shadow Monk Under-Robe
fact: Khell-Vire wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray — a sign he had not stopped dressing like what he was.
source_quote: He wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray, which told me more about him than the records would have. You don't stop dressing like what you were. You just layer something else over it.

subject: Brother Ferrath
fact: Brother Ferrath (or possibly Brother Aldas) taught a class on the difference between solutions and postponements — and Zalthir remembers nothing else from it.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements. I remember nothing else from that class.

subject: The Spy's Demand for Formal Imprisonment
fact: The spy turned to Kalan and announced: 'I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.'
source_quote: The spy, for her part, was furious. She turned to Kalan and announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: Candlekeep Gate
fact: At Candlekeep's gate, the party had to open their bag to show Glabbagool and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy — which triggered the Gate Warden's intervention.
source_quote: When we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him...

subject: Zalthir's Realization About the Blind Monk's Question
fact: Zalthir realized that Khell-Vire wasn't asking what he knew — he was asking what he had become through what he'd lived.
source_quote: I found this genuinely interesting. Not the answer — there wasn't one — but the structure of the question. Khell-Vire wasn't asking what Zalthir knew. He was asking what Zalthir had *become* through what he'd lived.

subject: The Final Note on the Spy
fact: The spy and Glabbagool became great friends — she screamed about the meditation, but they talked.
source_quote: He said they'd become great friends.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by Khell-Vire as the one who built something better in spite of the manual, and whose combination of shadow step and hit is the most interesting thing about him.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire announced the award of a specialized shadow technique — three options, presented carefully, with the honest note that adjustments might be needed if any proved mechanically unfortunate.
source_quote: Although your skills are weak, clearly showing a lack of focus and training. There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement. And it is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is addressed directly by Philemon as a sentient being who needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight, and then, when ready, to grieve.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon confirmed we were enrolled in a two-stage process, and accepted the way I accept most things I've already decided to do: by not arguing about it.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz told Sister Yvenne the truth about his amnesia, his escape from the Underdark, and his unexplained headache, offering everything he knew in exchange for information.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's study
fact: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.
source_quote: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: The sage produced a vial of Resonant Slime. Glabbagool was very pleased.
source_quote: The sage produced a vial of Resonant Slime.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: Thorin, helpfully: 'Pocket Drow.'
source_quote: Thorin, helpfully: 'Pocket Drow.'

subject: Zalthir's shadow punch through the shadows
fact: Zalthir recalled something from the Underdark — a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut. He proposed showing that. He warned the blind monk, then executed it. His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.
source_quote: Zalthir recalled something from the Underdark — a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut.

subject: Daz's truth-telling in the Hall of Divination
fact: Daz told Sister Yvenne the truth about his amnesia, his escape from the Underdark, and his unexplained headache, offering everything he knew in exchange for information.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Dawnbringer's silence in Philemon's study
fact: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind. The kind where the thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind. The kind where the thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan trains you for the ledger — who owes whom, who knows what, who has already lost and hasn't noticed — and to notice when a word doesn't fit.
source_quote: The first thing Menzoberranzan trains you for is the ledger. Who owes whom, who knows what, who has already lost and hasn't noticed. The second thing Menzoberranzan trains you for — and this one is equally useful but considerably less comfortable — is to notice when a word doesn't fit.

subject: gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions
fact: A sage of xenobiology approached, apparently drawn by the news of a gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions.
source_quote: Is it true you are teaching a gelatinous cube the way of the shadow?

subject: spider thing
fact: Daz was locked up with a few people in a jail because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep them.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: The combination of shadow step and hit
fact: The way forward was in the combination.
source_quote: Then he said the way forward was in the combination.

subject: The truth-telling exchange in the Hall of Divination
fact: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: The two-stage process for Dawnbringer
fact: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.

subject: the moment Zalthir chose option C
fact: Zalthir chose option C.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: the moment Daz told the truth in the Hall of Divination
fact: I told her the truth.
source_quote: I told her the truth.

subject: the moment Dawnbringer went quiet in Philemon's study
fact: Dawnbringer went quiet.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a shortened form of Daz'issin, a softening name mothers use for boys they wish to live, and is not commonly used in the past three centuries.
source_quote: Daz'issin, lit. small shadow

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan teaches individuals to read rooms and watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan teaches you to read rooms. It teaches you to watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.

subject: Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldry book with a mechanically removed appendix that referenced a footnote about Daz'issin.
source_quote: Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe. Two hundred years old, give or take. The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor.

subject: removal of appendix from Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe
fact: Someone used a razor at least fifty years ago to remove the appendix referenced by a footnote about Daz'issin, indicating deliberate erasure of information.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: library with all the information in the world
fact: A library that, by reputation, holds all the information in the world, yet contains something that should be here but is not, indicating a deliberate act of omission.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: struck fourth seat in Menzoberranzan
fact: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan, and when struck, it is not merely a political erasure but an expensive, infrastructure-dependent act requiring knowledge of the right people and payment that leaves no trace.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne maintains a practiced stillness inconsistent with her words, indicating she knows more than the public record allows her to say and is carefully navigating rather than simply informing.
source_quote: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes. The practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: erasure of houses that used the name Daz'issin
fact: Most houses that used the name Daz'issin did not last, suggesting systemic suppression or destruction linked to the name's use.
source_quote: The houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: room where public record is sealed
fact: The room contains a sealed public record, and the person within it is the current embodiment of that record, unable to speak of what is forbidden.
source_quote: The public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: Daz's realization of possible maternal naming
fact: Daz realizes his name may have been given by his mother as a softening form — Daz'issin — intended to ensure his survival, and that this naming may be connected to a suppressed lineage.
source_quote: Well, isn't my name, Daz? Maybe it's my full name? I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.
